scene_translation: Hundreds of people move through the high-ceilinged concourse of Tokyo Station. And yet, a single elderly man standing near one of the pillars stares directly at you without moving. He slowly approaches and says in a low voice, "You saw something at the station exit, didn't you. That envelope — it was meant to reach you." Gripped in his right hand is a small scrap of paper, written on in the same blue ink.
grammar_note: 【〜べき】 The man says とどくべきものだった — 'it was something that was supposed to reach you.' べき attaches to the plain verb form and expresses that something ought to happen or was destined to happen. It carries a sense of obligation or inevitability. Note also his rough, older-male register: だろ and ～ぞ at the end of sentences, rather than the polite ～ですね or ～ましたか you'd hear from a shopkeeper.

mystery_memo: The central mystery: テスト is being sought out — someone, or something, has been arranging for an envelope (spotted at the station exit in scene 1) to reach them. The elderly man at the pillar knows テスト's name without being introduced and knows they saw the envelope, suggesting surveillance or foreknowledge. He carries a second scrap of paper written in the same blue ink as the envelope, hinting at a connected sender or system. NPC relationship — Old Man at Pillar: neutral/watchful; he is not hostile but speaks roughly, as if テスト should already know what is happening. His significance and identity remain unknown.
